checks.name: case folding, which is the other half of rule one
checks.expect_failure: an uppercase handle is folded to the live lowercase one
checks._why: The first version of this mutation flipped the character class in stripIllegal from [^a-z0-9-] to [^a-zA-Z0-9-] and SURVIVED, because toLowerCase runs first and no uppercase letter ever reaches it. The battery reported the survivor, which is what a survivor is for. The guard that actually does the work is the case fold, so that is what is broken here.

checks.name: undoing by position rather than by string replace
checks.replace: for (const s of spans) undone = undone.split(s.to).join(s.from);

checks._why: The bug the first version shipped with. ap-csa-lesson-4-1 links lesson 4-5 correctly in one place and with a newline in the handle in another, so a string replace turns the good link into a broken one and refuses a page it should repair.

checks.name: a SECOND implementation, in another language, asking a different question
checks._why: The generator records spans and reverses them. This blanks every href out of the before and the after body and requires what is left to be identical, which is one statement that nothing outside a link attribute moved and does not care how the edit was made. It keeps its OWN copy of the retarget map rather than importing it, so a new entry is refused until a person agrees with it twice. Mutation-tested against a byte changed outside a href, an invented target, an unmapped retarget, a plausible but wrong typo repair, a wrong Command and a no-op row.

checks.name: the sheet clears the preflight, with every emoji round-tripped against the live body
checks.command: node -e "const fs=require('fs'),os=require('os'),path=require('path');const D='smoke/fixtures/dead-link-bodies';const out={};for(const f of fs.readdirSync(D))if(f.endsWith('.html'))out[f.slice(0,-5)]=fs.readFileSync(path.join(D,f),'utf8');const t=path.join(os.tmpdir(),'dead-link-carrying.json');fs.writeFileSync(t,JSON.stringify(out));console.log(t);" > /tmp/carrying-path.txt && node scripts/matrixify-preflight.js imports/2026-09-02/dead-link-repair-pages.csv --carrying "$(cat /tmp/carrying-path.txt)"
checks._why: The preflight reads the FILE rather than the intention: BOM, CRLF, QUOTE_ALL, a recognisable filename, Command, cell limits, and the blank-cell rule. Passing the live bodies as --carrying is what separates an emoji this sheet ADDED from one it round-tripped; without it the sheet is refused, which is the correct default.

checks.name: the storefront no longer serves a link to nothing on these three pages
checks.command: node -e "const cp=require('child_process');const want=[['ap-csa-lesson-4-1-ethical-social-issues-data-collection',[],['%0A']],['ap-csa-lesson-1-1-intro-algorithms',['Start daily practice'],['/pages/ap-csa-daily-practice']],['ap-csa-lesson-1-2-variables-data-types',['Start daily practice'],['/pages/ap-csa-daily-practice']]];for(const [h,present,absent] of want){const html=cp.execSync('curl -sSL --max-time 40 --compressed https://www.apcsexamprep.com/pages/'+h,{encoding:'utf8',maxBuffer:1<<26});for(const s of present)if(!html.includes(s))throw new Error(h+' no longer carries '+JSON.stringify(s));for(const s of absent)if(html.includes(s))throw new Error(h+' still serves '+JSON.stringify(s));}console.log('STOREFRONT LINKS RESOLVE on 3 of 3 repaired pages');"
checks._why: The ABSENT assertions are the ones that are false today and cannot pass without the import: the lesson 4-1 page serves two hrefs with %0A inside the handle, and both Unit 1 lesson pages serve a Start daily practice button pointing at /pages/ap-csa-daily-practice, which is a 404. The PRESENT assertion is deliberately not the proof, because the rendered page already links /pages/daily-practice eight times from the theme chrome; it is here so that deleting the button instead of repointing it cannot pass either. A first draft of this check asserted /pages/daily-practice was present and would have passed before the import, on chrome alone, which is the decoration this gate exists to refuse.
